## About this deck

This deck exercises every surface of the `ssus-slides` format: the blueprint
hero you just saw, the heading hierarchy, list treatments, a figure in the
lab's series palette, booktabs tables, math in MathJax, columns, a callout,
and a citation.

The grammar follows the brand identity sheets: a mono eyebrow carries the
series line, the title is set heavy in Libre Franklin, and detail lines stay
muted. Chrome is four corners only.

## Type hierarchy {#type}

### A level-three heading

Body text set at the deck root — 32 px so dense slides stay legible from the
back row. **Bold** and *italic* carry inline emphasis; a
[link](https://spatialscience.org) goes ink-blue with a graticule underline.

#### A level-four annotation label

For asides and block labels — the masthead's mono grammar, not an italic
accent.

> A quotation, quiet: graticule rule, secondary voice.

## A figure in the series palette

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: 68%
#| fig-height: 2.6
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "serif",
    "figure.dpi": 150,
})
SERIES = ["#0467A8", "#E0691E", "#14938D", "#AC8205", "#914A8C", "#58994A"]
x = np.linspace(0, 10, 200)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 2.4))
for i, c in enumerate(SERIES):
    ax.plot(x, (x * (i + 1) ** 0.5) % 8 + i * 0.4, color=c, lw=2, label=f"series {i + 1}")
ax.set_xlabel("x")
ax.set_ylabel("f(x)")
ax.legend(frameon=False, ncols=2, fontsize=8)
plt.show()
```

The six lab series, as matplotlib draws them. Data colors only — the palette
is validated for colorblind and contrast-safe use, and Signal (series 2)
stays out of the mark and the chrome.

## Math

Comparative spatial inference permutes the assignment vector to build a null
distribution of the difference $\hat{D}^{*}_b$. The permutation $p$-value
estimates

$$p = \frac{1}{B}\,\sum_{b=1}^{B} \mathbb{1}\!\left( \lvert \hat{D}^{*}_b \rvert \geq \lvert \hat{D} \rvert \right)$$

Inline, $\tilde{H}$ decomposes additively across the city–suburb partition.

::: {.column width="58%"}
**The argument.** Zoning is a municipal instrument: its effect operates
through competition among *intra*-metropolitan jurisdictions, the sorting the
Tiebout mechanism describes.
